prompt:
tomlkit.parse accepts documents that define the same table twice when an unrelated table sits in between:

from tomlkit import parse
doc = parse("[a]
b.c = 1
[zz]
q = 9
[a.b]
d = 2
")
print(doc.unwrap())

This prints {'a': {'b': {'c': 1, 'd': 2}}, 'zz': {'q': 9}} with no error. stdlib tomllib.loads rejects the same text with TOMLDecodeError: Cannot declare ('a', 'b') twice (at line 5, column 5), because b.c = 1 already defines table a.b.

A similar document where b is a plain value also parses without error and only fails later:

doc = parse("[a]
b = true
[zz]
q = 9
[a.b]
arr = [1, 2]
")  # no error
doc.unwrap()  # KeyAlreadyPresent: Key "b" already exists.

tomllib rejects that one too (Cannot overwrite a value). Without the [zz] table in between, tomlkit already raises for both. I expected parse() to raise ParseError for both documents, while valid out-of-order tables such as "[a]
x=1
[zz]
[a.b]
c=1
" keep parsing and round-tripping.

prompt_original:
fix: reject out-of-order concrete+super table redefinitions at parse time (#530)

Out-of-order value-vs-table and dotted-key-vs-table redefinitions
were silently accepted (or only raised on access) because the inner
if-elif chain in Container.append had no else clause for the case
where an existing concrete table is extended by a super-table after
an unrelated table header.

- Add else clause that validates the super-table against the concrete
  table, catching type mismatches and double table definitions at parse
  time instead of lazily during access/unwrap.
- Enhance _validate_table_candidate to detect when a non-dotted
  candidate key is a prefix of an existing dotted key.
- Call _validate_out_of_order_table after _raw_append in the fallthrough
  path so out-of-order fragments are validated before the document is
  materialized.

Fixes #523
